topic.title: A prince planned a 170 km desert city for 1.5 million people; the 2030 plan is 2.4 km

title: Saudi Arabia planned a 170 km city. Then it shrank 🏜️
description:
Can a reported $1.5T project build any city you dream of?
The Line was planned 170 km long; in 2024 the target for 2030 shrank to 2.4 km, and work has since been put on hold.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: What would you build with that money? Comment

lines.text: You think money builds any city? Not this one. Here's why.
Saudi Arabia planned The Line, one straight city 170 kilometres long.
It was meant to house 1.5M people by the end of the decade.
Neom's reported price tag: $1.5T. So what could stop it?
Every kilometre has to be dug, poured and glassed in. So how far did they get?
Then the plan was cut: just 2.4 kilometres this decade, 1.4% of the line. Now even that is on hold.
Because a price tag of $1.5T is a plan, not money in the bank.
So, still think money builds any city?

Out of date (beat 'turn', title, description): the 2.4 km by 2030 figure (Bloomberg, Apr 2024; confirmed on hospitalitynet.org/news/4121311.html) has been superseded. Semafor exclusive 22 May 2026 ('Saudi's NEOM halts work on The Line until after 2030', semafor.com) reports work on The Line halted until after 2030 and the 2030 population target cut to up to 100,000; repeated by Domus (27 May 2026), New Atlas (Jun 2026), Parametric Architecture. 'By the decade's end, just 2.4 kilometres' and the title 'By 2030: 2.4 km' now state a 2030 outcome the latest reporting contradicts; retell with current figures (sourced) or as the 2024 cut followed by the 2026 halt.

Misattributed fact (beat 'people', 'payoff'): 'Its budget: a reported $1.5T' attaches the $1.5T to The Line, but the source (Bloomberg headline) gives $1.5T for the whole Neom project, not The Line. Say 'Neom, the $1.5T project The Line belongs to' or similar; the payoff '$1.5T buys the plan' has the same problem.

Confirmed on the source page: 170 km, 2.4 km by 2030 (as of Apr 2024), 1.5M residents once hoped, fewer than 300,000 (Apr 2024); $1.5T only in the headline, for Neom overall. Disclaimer present in description; no advice, tone fine.
Plan passes the variety rules.

Misleading conclusion (beat 'payoff', also 'hook'/'loop' framing): 'Because a $1.5T project buys the plan, not the years it takes to build' says the cut happened for lack of time despite ample money. Sources say otherwise: Bloomberg/Hospitality Net (Apr 2024) gives no reason; Semafor (22 May 2026) ties the halt to cost ('to make NEOM less costly to develop'), PIF shifting spending to ports and data centres, budget deficits and weak foreign investment. The $1.5T was a reported cost, not money in hand, so 'money can't buy years' is not supported. Retell the payoff around cost/funding (e.g. a $1.5T price tag is a plan, not money in the bank) or drop the causal 'Because'.

Same issue on screen and voice: 'ask' says the project 'had a reported $1.5T' and the payoff card labels it 'Budget'; the source gives $1.5T only as the project's headline size/cost. Say 'a reported $1.5T price tag' / label 'Reported cost'.

Confirmed: 170 km, 1.5M residents once hoped by 2030, 2.4 km by 2030 as of Apr 2024 (hospitalitynet.org/news/4121311.html, Bloomberg); 'now even that is on hold' confirmed by Semafor 22 May 2026 (work on The Line halted until at least after 2030), repeated by Domus and New Atlas. $1.5T now correctly tied to the whole Neom project. Disclaimer in description; no advice; tone fine. Style: spoken 'a one point five trillion dollars project' reads awkwardly.
